inspection_summary: Verified the frozen SHA-256 and 929-line count, then inspected every line. The source develops a conditional moment-to-gap method: Hardy's real Z-function represents critical-line zeros, random-matrix moment conjectures supply separate function and derivative constants, and three endpoint Wirtinger inequalities turn a hypothetical uniform gap cap into explicit lower bounds. Fresh units also retain the distinctions among pair correlation, all-zero normalized limsup gaps, critical-line gaps, and positive-proportion multi-zero gaps. Garbled formula tables are isolated as extraction-defective rather than treated as exact evidence.

accepted_units.title: Hardy Z turns critical-line zero geometry into a real-variable moment problem
accepted_units.why_material: The phase-adjusted Hardy function is real on the real axis, preserves the critical-line modulus, and has zeros exactly at critical-line zeta zeros; defining moments of Z and Z' then makes zero spacing accessible to real endpoint inequalities.
accepted_units.context_note: The surrounding zeta definition and functional equation are background; this span includes the representation, zero correspondence, and both moment families needed downstream.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the displayed phase factor and integral notation, but the prose makes the representation and moment roles recoverable despite extraction noise.

accepted_units.title: Mixed RMT moments expose a coefficient-availability bottleneck
accepted_units.why_material: The source connects zeta moments to random-matrix constants and explains that the mixed-moment route requires rational functions H(h,k) whose unavailable values beyond the known range block higher-k gap estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly conjectural input, not verified zeta asymptotics; the terminal prose identifies the obstruction and motivates the later change of moment representation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual relation and bottleneck are recoverable from prose. Exact rational formulas in lines 189-218 are OCR-fragile and require scan verification; they are not relied on as exact values here.

accepted_units.title: Separate derivative moments replace unavailable mixed-moment coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Characteristic-polynomial derivative moments motivate a conjecture for M_k with constants c_k, offering a separate derivative/function moment ratio that can be inserted into gap inequalities without computing H(h,k).
accepted_units.context_note: The source says c_k is available explicitly through k=15 and defers those values to the main-results section.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The determinant/combinatorial formula in lines 248-271 is extraction-fragile, but the prose securely supports the existence, origin, and finite availability of c_k.

accepted_units.title: Pair correlation is a distributional spacing lens distinct from extremal gaps
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates the large-gap objective from pair correlation, while relating the latter to essential simplicity and unitary eigenvalue statistics; this prevents treating all zero-spacing evidence as the same target.
accepted_units.context_note: The pair-correlation statement is introductory context rather than an ingredient in the paper's three proofs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on a normalized pair-count display, but the complementary role and spectral analogy are stated in checked prose.

accepted_units.title: Normalized gaps define separate limsup and liminf extremal statistics
accepted_units.why_material: Dividing consecutive ordinate gaps by 2pi/log(gamma_n) creates a scale-free sequence with average one, after which lambda and mu isolate asymptotically large and small gaps.
accepted_units.context_note: The later list of historical numerical bounds supports context but adds no new mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on the displayed normalization and limsup/liminf definitions, which are legible and reinforced by prose.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line gap Lambda dominates the all-zero gap statistic and coincides with it under RH
accepted_units.why_material: Defining Lambda using distinct positive critical-line zeros clarifies what the real Hardy-function argument can measure; Lambda is at least lambda unconditionally at the definitional level described here, and the distinction disappears under RH.
accepted_units.context_note: The span also records the first cited Beesack-Wirtinger lower-bound instance as evidence that endpoint inequalities can address this target.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the displayed normalized limsup definition and one numerical bound; both relations are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Moment information and stronger variational Wirtinger inequalities successively sharpen gap bounds
accepted_units.why_material: The historical progression shows two independent levers in the same proof family: richer mixed moments and stronger endpoint inequalities, including a variational inequality whose optimization can be recast algebraically through Jacobi-Schur functions.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is comparative evidence for the reusable method architecture, not a new proof of the cited bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several moment displays are formula-dependent; their exact coefficients are readable only with caution, while the method comparisons are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Global-versus-local averages yield positive-proportion multi-zero gap statements
accepted_units.why_material: This route compares a continuous global average with a discrete local average and targets r-step gaps for a positive proportion of zeros, rather than only an extremal limsup.
accepted_units.context_note: It is a cited alternative, not used in the main proofs, and remains conditional on RH and the stated moment conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The quantitative threshold is display-dependent, but the averaging mechanism and positive-proportion conclusion are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: The paper reframes higher-k gap extension around separately available b_k and c_k
accepted_units.why_material: After recording the prior mixed-moment ceiling, the source proposes using ordinary Hardy moments and derivative moments with explicit b_k and c_k to continue from k=7 through k=15.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the bridge from the literature review to the three main theorem instantiations; the advertised numerical conclusion is conditional on RH and the moment predictions.
